brief:
Adnan Barq, a 25-year-old Palestinian journalist and filmmaker from Jerusalem's Old City, was an infant when the Durban Conference convened a quarter-century ago. Amnesty International marked the anniversary by featuring Barq's perspective on the international gathering, which brought together activists and advocates focused on human rights concerns.

Barq expressed interest in examining how the conference mobilized such broad participation around shared commitments to human rights work. He noted the significance of observing the scale and scope of coordination that characterized the event, particularly in retrospect from the vantage point of someone born during that pivotal moment in advocacy history.

title: Palestinian journalist reflects on Durban Conference legacy 25 years later
